absent: Whether callers must hold address space lock for insertion helpers beyond the internal assertions observed
Exact layout and lifetime of translation gather state and notifier internals
Recursion details for lower-level copy helpers beneath top-level walk
Cache attribute selection rules for frame tracking beyond success or failure
Reference counting and reverse mapping lifecycle for special versus normal entries after insertion
Concurrency rules for concurrent faults on the same address during upgrade

findings.text: Fork helper for a virtual range that skips table duplication when faults can rebuild entries, delegates huge page areas elsewhere, and otherwise walks top entries copying each populated branch while reporting allocation exhaustion on failure.

Reaping helper that clears all mappings of a given area for teardown, gathering translation state and attempting nonblocking invalidation first, abandoning with a busy signal when invalidation cannot proceed without waiting.

Range unmapper that removes translations spanning one or more areas between caller supplied bounds, clamping each area to the requested span and surrounding the whole walk with invalidation while marking entries for drop and unmap.

Guarded clearer for device or mixed mappings that silently returns unless the requested span lies inside the area and the area carries raw frame or mixed mode, otherwise delegating to the generic range clearer.

Table walker that ensures intermediate levels exist down to the leaf parent and then returns the locked leaf entry for a given address, reporting absence when any allocation fails and asserting that huge leaf state is absent.

Public insertion helpers that map caller supplied pages into a virtual area, promoting the area to mixed mode when needed and validating coverage before delegating to a batched leaf installer that tracks how many pages remain unmapped.

Object mappers that cover an entire area from an array with either area-relative or zero-based offset, rejecting offsets beyond the array end or arrays shorter than the area before delegating to the batched insertion helper.

Split kernel mapping pair where preparation promotes descriptor state to mixed mode and checks coverage without installing entries, while completion performs the actual batched insertion using the area protection.

Fault-time frame installer that validates mapping mode exclusivity and address bounds plus permission allowance and cache attributes, then installs a special frame entry and reports no-page on success with bus or allocation signals on failure.

Fault-time mixed installers that accept either raw frames or structured pages, enforcing zero-frame policy and bounds and cachemode before choosing frame or page paths and translating kernel error signals into fault codes while treating busy as benign.

Copy decision where duplication is required when the destination carries copy-on-fork mode or the source has anonymous state implying non-rebuildable tables, while shareable or read-only ranges without such state are left for later fault fill to lighten fork cost.

Shared zero page policy that forbids insertion when the address space opts out, broadly permits it for copy-on-write or non-writable areas, and otherwise permits it only when the area offers a write-commit hook combined with direct storage or device character.

Pre-insert validation that rejects pages lacking references as well as anonymous or typed pages, conditionally accepts the shared zero page per policy without further work, and otherwise flushes processor cache for the folio before allowing installation.

Occupied leaf policy where a populated entry causes busy without upgrade intent, while upgrade intent requires the existing frame to match the requested page and then marks the entry young with write and access updates, treating mismatch as a fault signal.

Remap contract requiring aligned start and pre-validated area flags, empty leaf entries throughout the span, per-frame permission allowance, and cache flushing of the range before table descent, with any violation aborting the walk.

Tracking split where full-area coverage allocates a persistent context attached to the area and rejects duplicate contexts, while partial coverage only adjusts cache attributes, with release untracking the span and freeing the context.

Fork copy protection where copy-on-write sources are surrounded by invalidation notifications and a raw sequence guard under asserted write lock, ensuring secondary mappings observe permission downgrade while avoiding preemption complaints.

Teardown notification discipline where reaping uses gathered translation state with a nonblocking start that can fail busy, while bulk unmap uses blocking start and end around iteration over each intersecting area.

Leaf locking where insertion and remap paths hold the leaf lock across each small batch or range, allocating upper levels beforehand with a single upper lock, enabling lazy translation mode during bulk fill and releasing after each batch.

Teardown descriptors observed as a flag bundle selecting reaping versus drop-marker plus unmap behavior, a notifier span carrying type and address space with start and end, and an unmap iterator carrying first area plus global bounds and tree cursor.

Mapping descriptors observed as a tracking context holding base frame plus length with reference counting, and a kernel action holding start plus page count with page array, consumed by prepare and complete stages.

Batched insertion progresses across leaf tables from the start address, filling bounded groups under one lock at a time, advancing address and index on success, and on any failure unwinding the current group count into a remaining total for the caller.

Remap tracking lifecycle moves from attribute setup or context allocation through table fill to either attachment of the context to the area on success or release of the context on failure, with later release untracking and freeing.

Mixed insertion selects frame path when special entries are available or the frame lacks structure, otherwise translating the frame to a structured page and using the page path, then mapping exhaustion and invalid cases to fault signals.

Hazards include partial table fill leaving uncounted frames that must be cleared promptly on error, races between block allocation and invalidation causing frame mismatch that must skip upgrade rather than overwrite, and long-term pinning of shared zero pages against later replacement.

Completion signals observed are allocation exhaustion, busy, bad address, invalid argument, access denial, and offset beyond object for kernel callers, plus fault codes for no-page success, allocation failure, and bus error for fault handlers.

Mode and notification selectors observed govern copy-on-fork, raw frame versus mixed mappings, writability and device character, protection versus clear versus unmap invalidation, drop-marker with unmap clearing, and remap flag preconditions.

Coverage checks require the requested span to lie inside the area for single and batched inserts and remap-like clears, and require offset and length to fit within the supplied array for whole-area object mapping, otherwise reporting bad address or beyond-object.

Large page handling delegates fork duplication for huge areas to a dedicated helper, brackets bulk unmap per area with huge-aware begin and end hooks, and asserts absence of huge leaf state when walking to or allocating the leaf parent.

Table walk hazards include encountering corrupt top entries that are skipped after clearing, and unexpected huge leaves at the leaf parent level that trigger diagnostic assertions rather than silent handling.
Reference release helper for tracking contexts that removes cache tracking for the stored span and then frees the context memory, serving as the drop callback for the associated reference counter.
